Stan Lee weighs in on Michael B. Jordan as the Human Torch in 'Fantastic Four'

If they were real people then it would be strange to change their races or genders, but since these are works of fiction it is always appropriate to update and reinterpret. As an artist it almost goes without saying that Stan Lee would understand this about his brain child. Imagine if we never updated Shakespeare's plays to reflect the times. They would be unintelligible and lose meaning. Worse still imagine if we were to forget their original form, then they would be equally meaningless. Knowing that we are looking at a black man in what was a white character is part of what makes this new version important. If it were verbatim or if we didn't know what the original looked like dit would lose all that meaning.

To be honest the only thing I hated when this casting came out was that sue, who is supposed to be his sister, was white. And it looks like they give us an explanation and now I'm ok with it. Plus it's Michael B Jordan. Right now I can't imagine anyone else playing that part but him, he's the perfect fit
Looks as though Sue is the adopted one. They can give a one line Throw away on that and that's all I need

Came here to say exactly this. I'm fine with the casting, but when it was first announced they did a terrible job of explaining it. My first reaction wasn't WTF he's black?? It was, WTF how is he black and his sister is still white?? Are they not siblings anymore? No they clearly say she's his sister. So is he adopted? Is she adopted?

These are existing characters so if you're going to just start messing with the back story of some beloved literary figures with some hardcore fans, you better explain! Since they were already messing with these characters by making them teenagers, people were on edge, and I think this drove them over the edge. It had nothing to do with race and everything to do with changing an existing franchise some fans are invested in. That's kind of the deal you agree to when you decide to go make a comic book movie, you're going to be dealing with fanboys.

I completely understand the change, and the article tries to make it a race thing. It's not though. It's the 'joker' problem; everyone grows up with a different version of the joker. Every time someone tries to reinterpret the character there's a large out cry of, 'that's not the joker'. It's because the archetype that they have of the joker is not completely what that joker is. It happens with every interpretation of some other source material, and everybody will forget about it if the movie is good... if it's bad that could be something they blame it on.

It's the catch 22 of all adaptations of source material, if you don't change it somewhere then what is the point of re-making it? Apparently it was perfect in its previous forms so why bother redoing it? If you change it too much then you obviously don't respect/love the source material, so again, why are you bothering to remake it? You're damned if you do and damned if you don't. But you knew that going into it, making a comic book movie, so I have no sympathy if you catch flack over it.

It's just in this case the fanboy whining was interpreted as racism. Not saying there aren't shitty people out there who are legitimately racist, but come on it's a comic book movie! 95% of the complaining is coming from fanboys hating on you changing something they love. It's like when Nicolas Cage was going to play Superman, people were outraged.
